mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the next month reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day period.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 30-day period of stable rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in union membership (not directly observable but proxy via labor market tightness indicators) weakens consumer confidence, which precedes a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by at least 2% in one month
failure_condition: Confidence index (e.g., U.S. Manufacturing Sentiment Index) shows no significant decline and 5-day returns are non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP deflator inflation (CPIAUCSL) surprises exceed +0.5% in the current month, it anticipates a future tightening of monetary policy, which drives a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during periods of CPIAUCSL changes <= 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) signals supply-side weakness that lags into equity markets, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior 30-day average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment (PAYEMS) coupled with persistently low consumer credit (not directly observable) create a risk-on environment that drives a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for two consecutive months
regime_hint: labor market weakening without credit collapse
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative despite a rising trend in monthly PAYEMS over the prior 6 months (Slopesign p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% for the first time in three months, it indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts investor sentiment and drives a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% and remains below for the next 30 days
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive in the following 10 days (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in retail sales (not directly observable but proxy via HOUST) and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests shifting demand composition toward consumer goods, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 2% while INDPRO decreases by 1% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during periods of neutral demand (HOUST flat and INDPRO stable) (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent supply chain disruptions (proxy via INDPRO not improving for three months), the S&P 500 anticipates future disruptions by underperforming in the next 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO does not improve for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than the prior 30-day average (p > 0.10).
